principles.text: When real selling shows up (a leader closing below its breakout-day low with a 3-day reversal, mega-caps 50% above the 50 EMA on huge volume), reduce exposure; don't buy the dip even when it gaps down into the EMAs.
On a gap-down day, don't panic-sell the whole book at once; scale out and prefer selling into any bounce rather than dumping into weakness.
Don't short too early; if it's a short-term top the market likely needs to spend time up there before turning, so wait rather than initiate shorts into the first drop.

After a prolonged 2-month uptrend, a pullback has a higher chance of being a deeper/longer consolidation than the quick sideways-then-up that occurs early in a trend (e.g. ARM in April after only 2-3 weeks up).
To recover from an over-trading death spiral, recognizing the over-trading is the first step; then take a break, stop watching the market, and evaluate your trades.
On the strongest holders still in an uptrend, wait for a final blow-off push (like ARM/Marvell did) and sell into that strength rather than exiting early.
